statement: One accent hue, carried only by meaningful inline elements (tags, links, live indicators); chrome stays achromatic but hue-linked, and elevation stays under 8px blur at low alpha.
mechanismHypothesis: When color appears only where it encodes meaning, the eye can use color as a reliable retrieval signal — a teal token IS a tag, everywhere. Tinting the grays toward the accent hue (obs-mew-tokens/f3) keeps the achromatic chrome from reading as a second, colder palette, which is how surfaces acquire visual noise without any single loud element.
appliesWhen: text-dominant surfaces where inline metadata must be scannable
dark-first products where saturation fatigues quickly
doesNotApplyWhen: data visualization surfaces needing categorical palettes (dataviz skill governs there)
status-heavy dashboards where semantic red/amber/green carry meaning the accent cannot
confidenceBasis: Derived from one source-grounded positive (owner-owned Mew checkout, file:line locators) plus Mobbin counterexamples; no audience-task evidence yet, so confidence is capped below audience-proven per the M-tier rule.
reVerifyReason: Mew is under active development in the owner-local checkouts and Mobbin comparators drift with product releases; re-inspect the live surfaces and re-read global.css before continuing to cite these facts.
tierLadder: M2: live shipped-product observation (owner-owned source checkout with file:line locators, plus Mobbin live screens). M1 documentation not consulted. M3 audience-task evidence absent — no rule here may be promoted to audience-proven until a real capture task is observed.
